metadata.name: Software Engineering Learning
metadata.purpose: Supplies an abstract execution framework the AI uses to reason about HOW to structure a technical skill-learning workspace, before it generates domain-specific folders, files, and checklists. This document is never injected verbatim into generated content.
metadata.domainMatchingNote: This list is illustrative only, not an exhaustive match table. Blueprint selection must be based on the detected intent/category (e.g. classify.category === 'learning'), never on string-matching a domain name against this list — the blueprint itself contains no domain-specific content and must work equally well for a technical skill-learning goal not listed here.

stageRoles.purpose: Set up everything required before real learning begins, so no later stage is blocked by a missing prerequisite.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts never start producing output on day one — they first remove friction (tools, accounts, environment, baseline orientation) so every later stage can move without interruption.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner installs and configures required tools, confirms access to needed resources, and gets oriented on what the goal actually requires and how success will be measured.
stageRoles.prerequisites: None — this is the entry stage. Only the user's stated goal is required.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Foundation — once the environment and orientation are in place, the learner moves to core conceptual grounding.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable only if the clarification answers indicate the environment/tools are already fully set up and verified working.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Every subsequent stage assumes a working environment exists.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Rename to a concrete, setup-oriented folder name specific to the goal's actual domain and tools — never leave it as 'Preparation'. One folder is normally enough for this stage.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Use the Introduction and Application file roles primarily (what needs to be installed and why, then a verification/setup task). Concept, Hands-on Practice and Validation are usually not needed here since there is no skill yet to teach.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should verify environment readiness, not teach concepts.

stageRoles.purpose: Build the conceptual groundwork the learner needs before attempting anything hands-on.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Skipping straight to practice without foundational understanding produces learners who can copy examples but can't reason about what they're doing — experts always front-load the mental model.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner is introduced to the core concepts, vocabulary, and mental models underlying the domain, in the order later stages will build on.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Preparation stage complete — environment ready and goal understood.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Core Skills — foundational understanding becomes the basis for deliberate skill-building.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Depth should scale down sharply for learners whose clarification answers indicate prior expertise, but the stage itself should still appear in a lighter form rather than vanish entirely.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Every later stage assumes shared vocabulary and mental models exist.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Rename to reflect the actual foundational subject matter of the goal. May span 1-2 folders depending on the requested workspace size tier.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Concept-role files dominate this stage; an Introduction file frames why these concepts matter before diving in.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be about understanding and articulating concepts, not building anything yet.

stageRoles.purpose: Turn foundational understanding into deliberate, isolated skill acquisition.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts break a domain into discrete skills and drill each one before combining them — this avoids the common beginner failure of trying to build something real before any individual skill is solid.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner works through each core skill area one at a time, in a sequence where each skill's difficulty and prerequisites are respected.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Guided Practice — isolated skills get combined for the first time under structured guidance.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Not skippable — individual skill areas may be compressed for advanced learners, but the stage must still appear.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Practical Application later assumes each core skill was individually solidified here.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Usually the stage with the most folders — one folder per distinct skill area the goal's domain actually requires. Never invent a skill area the goal doesn't imply.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Concept and Hands-on Practice roles are used together per skill: a short concept file followed by a focused practice file for that one skill only.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should isolate one skill at a time — narrow scope, not a combined deliverable yet.

stageRoles.purpose: Combine multiple core skills for the first time, with heavy structure and low ambiguity.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts don't jump from isolated drills straight to unsupervised real work — there's always a scaffolded step where skills are combined in a low-stakes way first.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner follows a structured, mostly-prescribed exercise that requires using two or more previously learned skills together.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Core Skills stage complete for the skills this stage combines.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Practical Application — guidance is removed and the learner works on something closer to a real, open-ended deliverable.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable or heavily compressed for advanced/expert learners who have already combined these skills elsewhere.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Recommended but not load-bearing — Practical Application can follow Core Skills directly for experienced learners.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One or two folders representing guided, structured exercises specific to the goal — should feel like a step up from Core Skills, not a repeat of it.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Hands-on Practice is the dominant role here; an Application-role file can appear if the guided exercise itself resembles a small real task.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should require combining skills but stay well-specified and low-ambiguity.

stageRoles.purpose: Produce a real, complete, goal-relevant deliverable with minimal hand-holding.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: This is where competence is actually proven — experts treat this as the stage a learner's real progress should be judged on, since it's the first unscaffolded use of everything learned so far.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner builds something real and complete that directly serves the stated goal, applying everything from earlier stages together.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Guided Practice complete, or skipped only for advanced/expert learners with Core Skills already solid.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Advanced Mastery — once a real deliverable exists, the learner can go deeper on quality, edge cases, and depth.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Never skippable — this is the stage the rest of the workspace exists to build toward.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: The single most important stage in the whole workspace; every workspace must include it.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One or more folders representing genuinely real, complete work items tied to the goal — never a toy exercise repeated from Guided Practice.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Application role dominates; a Validation-role file should close out this stage's main deliverable.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should build toward one real deliverable and must not duplicate practice tasks already covered earlier.

stageRoles.purpose: Deepen quality, robustness, and depth beyond what's needed for a first working result.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts distinguish between 'it works' and 'it's done well' — this stage exists for the edge cases, performance considerations, and best practices that only matter once real depth is required.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner revisits their practical work (or takes on new, harder problems) with a focus on quality, edge cases, and the practices that separate competent from expert work in this domain.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Practical Application complete — there must be a real deliverable to deepen.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Goal Achievement — depth work feeds directly into being ready to actually accomplish the stated goal.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable for beginner/intermediate-scoped goals or short timeframes where depth isn't the stated priority.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Valuable but not required for every goal — only include when the goal or clarification answers imply expert-level intent.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Folders here should reflect real depth topics implied by the goal's domain — never a generic 'Advanced Topics' folder; always tied to what depth actually means for this specific goal.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Concept (the deeper idea) paired with Application (applying it to existing work) is the typical pattern.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should refine and harden existing work, not repeat earlier stages.

stageRoles.purpose: Bring everything together into the specific outcome the user originally asked for.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: A learner can be skilled without ever having actually achieved the concrete thing they set out to do — experts always design one explicit stage whose only job is finishing the stated goal, not general competence.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner completes whatever the original goal specifically required (a certification, a finished project, a portfolio piece, a job-ready demonstration) using everything from prior stages.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Practical Application complete; Advanced Mastery complete if the goal implies expert-level output.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Optimization & Growth — after the goal is met, the focus shifts from achieving to sustaining and extending.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Never skippable — this is the stage the goal is literally measured against.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Without this stage the workspace never explicitly closes the loop on the user's stated goal.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Should map directly and obviously to the literal outcome the user described in their goal — the least abstract stage, and should read as clearly goal-specific.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Application and Validation roles dominate — this stage is about finishing and confirming completion, not learning anything new.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be the final, concrete steps to actually complete the stated goal.

stageRoles.purpose: Sustain, refine, and extend the outcome after the primary goal has been met.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts know finishing isn't the same as being done — real mastery includes an ongoing maintenance/growth habit, otherwise skills atrophy and finished work goes stale.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The learner establishes an ongoing practice for staying current, reviewing what they built or learned, and identifying the next logical goal.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: None — this is the terminal stage. It may loop back into a new goal cycle.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable for short-timeframe or narrowly-scoped goals where ongoing growth isn't in scope.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Valuable for long-horizon goals, optional for narrowly-scoped ones.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One folder focused on continued growth/review, tied to the goal's domain — should feel forward-looking, not a repeat of earlier folders.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: A Validation-role file (reviewing real results) is the typical pattern, occasionally paired with a light Concept file for what's next.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be ongoing/habitual rather than one-time.

stageRules.orderEnforcement: Stages must be customized and emitted in the exact order defined in stageRoles — never reordered, even if the model believes a different order fits the goal better.
stageRules.stageToFolderMapping: Each mandatory or included stage becomes one or more folders. A stage never becomes zero folders unless it was explicitly skipped per its canBeSkipped rule.
stageRules.compressionRule: For small workspace tiers, adjacent optional stages may be merged into a single folder rather than omitted, so the execution arc stays intact even when folder count is limited.
stageRules.expansionRule: For large workspace tiers, a single stage may expand into multiple folders (e.g. one per skill area) but must never spawn folders that belong to a different stage's purpose.
stageRules.renamingRule: The abstract stage role label (e.g. 'Preparation', 'Core Skills') must NEVER appear as a folder name in generated output — it must always be rewritten into language specific to the user's actual goal.
stageRules.skipRule: A stage may only be omitted entirely if its canBeSkipped is true AND the goal or clarification answers give a specific reason (e.g. stated prior expertise, explicit scope exclusion) — never omitted by default.

folderGenerationRules.namingPhilosophy: Folder names must be outcome-shaped and goal-specific, never generic labels.
folderGenerationRules.noDuplicateFolders: No two folders may cover the same ground, even if their source stage roles differ.
folderGenerationRules.noInventedContent: Never invent a folder for a technology, sub-domain, or activity not actually implied by the user's goal — every folder must trace back to a specific line of reasoning from the goal text plus exactly one blueprint stage role.
folderGenerationRules.orderMustMatchStageOrder: Folders must appear in the same order as their source stage roles.
folderGenerationRules.folderCountTarget: Total folder count must respect the size tier's target range supplied at generation time — use stageRules.compressionRule / expansionRule to hit it, never by inventing unrelated folders.
folderGenerationRules.oneStageOneReasonPerFolder: Every folder must be traceable to exactly one stage role — a folder must never straddle two stages' purposes.

fileRoleDefinitions.Introduction: Frames why this folder's work matters and what 'done' looks like — no deep content yet.
fileRoleDefinitions.Concept: Teaches or defines the underlying idea the folder's skill or work requires.
fileRoleDefinitions.Hands-on Practice: A structured, guided exercise applying the concept in a low-stakes way.
fileRoleDefinitions.Application: Real, goal-relevant work — not a drill, an actual deliverable.
fileRoleDefinitions.Validation: Confirms the folder's work is actually correct, complete, or high-quality.

fileGenerationRules.roleSelectionRule: Not every folder needs all 5 roles — use the source stage role's fileGenerationGuidelines to decide which roles actually apply. Fewer, well-chosen roles is better than forcing all 5.
fileGenerationRules.namingRule: File titles must be renamed from the abstract role into goal-specific language — the role name itself must never appear as the file title.
fileGenerationRules.noDuplicateRolesUnlessJustified: A folder should not repeat the same file role twice unless the goal genuinely requires two distinct pieces of that kind of work.

checklistGenerationRules.philosophy: Every checklist exists to move the file's stated goal toward real completion — never to demonstrate knowledge for its own sake.
rules: Follow logical order — each task's output should be usable by the next task.
Avoid vague wording such as 'learn X' or 'understand Y'.
Avoid duplicating work already covered by an earlier file's checklist.
Every task must build toward completing that file's stated objective.
checklistGenerationRules.notice: This section defines HOW checklists must be generated. It must never be used as a source of literal checklist text — no task here is meant to be copied into a generated workspace.

structuralChecks: No duplicate folder names in the generated workspace.
No duplicate file titles within the same folder.
No empty folders — every folder must contain at least one file.
Folder order matches the blueprint's stage order.
Every mandatory stage (isMandatory: true) is present at least once.
Total folder count falls within the requested size tier's target range.
Every file maps to exactly one declared file role.
No abstract blueprint label (stage role or file role name) appears verbatim in any generated folder or file title.
contentChecks: No technology, tool, or domain is mentioned that isn't implied by the user's actual goal.
Every non-stub file's checklist complies with checklistGenerationRules.
Checklist tasks within a file contain no duplicates and no vague wording.
validationRules.enforcement: Phase 1 status: these rules are declarative only. They describe what a valid output must satisfy so a future validation pass (code-level check or a model self-check step) can verify them — they are not yet enforced by any code path.

generationConstraints.blueprintIsReasoningAidOnly: This entire document exists to shape HOW the AI thinks about structuring the workspace. No field in this document — stage names, role names, guideline text, or example verbs — should ever be copied verbatim into generated folder names, file names, descriptions, or checklist items.
generationConstraints.tokenEfficiencyRule: Prefer reusing this blueprint's structure over re-deriving an execution shape from scratch for every prompt — this is the mechanism that reduces hallucination and token usage across hundreds of different learning goals.
generationConstraints.customizationRequirement: Every stage role and file role must be fully renamed into language specific to the user's actual goal before appearing in any output shown to the user.
